demo.title: Binomial with many slots against Poisson
demo.brief:
Single-file HTML demo showing the binomial distribution Bin(n, p = λ/n) converging to the Poisson distribution Poisson(λ) as n grows.

Concept: an hour is chopped into n equal time slots; each slot independently contains one event with probability λ/n (so the average number of events stays λ). The number of events X is Bin(n, λ/n). As n → ∞ this becomes Poisson(λ) with P(X=k) = e^{-λ} λ^k / k!.

Controls:
1. Slider "slots n": logarithmic scale, values 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 10000 (snap to these). Display current n. Must handle n < λ gracefully: if λ/n > 1, show a message "p = λ/n exceeds 1, need more slots" and grey out the binomial bars.
2. Slider "rate λ": from 0.5 to 10 in steps of 0.5, default 3.
3. Button "Simulate one hour": draws a horizontal timeline of the hour divided into n slots (if n > 200, draw just tick marks every so often and dots for events), samples each slot Bernoulli(λ/n), marks event slots with a dot, and shows "events this hour: X". Keep a running histogram of simulated counts below (button "Simulate 1000 hours" fills it fast; "Reset" clears it).

Main chart: bar chart for k = 0 to max(15, ceil(λ + 4·sqrt(λ))). For each k, two side-by-side bars: binomial P(X=k) for Bin(n, λ/n) (blue) and Poisson P(X=k) (orange). Y axis probability with gridlines. Legend. Hover a bar to see exact values to 4 decimals. Compute binomial probabilities with log-gamma or iteratively for numerical stability (n up to 10000). For k > n binomial probability is 0.

Readout panel: show p = λ/n; P(X=0) under binomial, i.e. (1 − λ/n)^n, next to e^{−λ}; and the largest absolute difference between the two PMFs over the shown k, labelled "max gap".

Style: clean, white background, sans-serif, readable on a laptop and a phone (responsive, stacked layout under 700px wide). Use plain text math like "(1 − λ/n)^n" and "e^(−λ)" or render with simple HTML superscripts; no external libraries required (vanilla JS + canvas or SVG).
